free_tier.stated: 'There's no additional charge for enabling code execution from the Gemini API.' card.summary: The free tier still exists and the pricing page still prints 'Free of charge' against input and output for Gemini 3.8 Flash, 3.6 Flash, 3.5 Flash-Lite, 3.1 F...

free_tier.stated: The free tier still exists and the pricing page still prints 'Free of charge' against input and output for Gemini 3.8 Flash, 3.6 Flash, 3.5 Flash-Lite, 3.1 Flash-Lite, 2.5 Flash-Lite and other models, and against context caching for Gemini 3.8 Flash and 3.6 Flash (2.5 Flash-Lite caching reads 'Not available'), but Google has stopped publishing how much the free tier carries. The rate-limits page now says only 'Rate limits depend on a variety of factors (such as your usage tier) and can be viewed in Google AI Studio', and the per-model free table the page carried through 2025 has been removed. The free columns that remain describe what is free, never how much. A Google AI Developers Forum post dated 2026-09-03 quotes 20 RPD on Gemini 3.8 Flash against 500 RPD on Flash-Lite.

The gap is the finding: a reader who trusts the word 'generous' on the pricing page and not the forum will design a batch that cannot run. card.summary: Free tier 1 GB of store; Tier 1 10 GB; Tier 2 100 GB; Tier 3 1 TB. 100 MB per document.

free_tier.stated: Free tier 1 GB of store; Tier 1 10 GB; Tier 2 100 GB; Tier 3 1 TB. 100 MB per document.

retention.stated: Raw files are deleted after 48 hours; only chunked embeddings persist, and there is no documented route to reassemble originals

egress.terms: Storage free, query-time embeddings free. You pay only indexing embeddings ($0.15 / 1M tokens) and context tokens on retrieval.

record.chaining: Multiple stores per project, but the project-wide total is the cap. 'File Search store size is computed on the backend … typically approximately 3 times the size of your input data'. So 1 TB of Tier 3 store ≈ 340 GB of input. On free tier, 1 GB store ≈ 333 MB of input.
record.limits_note: Per-object-cap 100 MB. 'Recommendation: Limit the size of each File Search store to under 20 GB'. No TTL on embeddings. They persist until manually deleted or the model is deprecated.
record.reliability_note: Raw files are automatically deleted after 48 hours, leaving only vector embeddings without endpoints to retrieve original source files. Free tier provides 1 GB of storage.

evidence.proved: 'Total size of project File Search stores (based on user tier): Free: 1 GB; Tier 1: 10 GB; Tier 2: 100 GB; Tier 3: 1 TB'; 'Maximum file size / per document limit: 100 MB'
'There is no Time To Live (TTL) for embeddings; they persist until manually deleted … Files, however, are deleted after 48 hours.'
'This is typically approximately 3 times the size of your input data'; 'Storage is free of charge.'

card.summary: 20 GB per project; 2 GB per file; 48-hour retention

free_tier.stated: 20 GB per project; 2 GB per file; 48-hour retention

retention.stated: 20 GB per project; 2 GB per file; 48-hour retention

egress.terms: Free. 'The Files API is available at no cost in all regions where the Gemini API is available.'.

record.tooling: pip install google-genai; curl multipart to /upload/v1beta/files
record.chaining: 20 GB/project, and Google Cloud projects are the multiplicative axis. But 48-hour retention means capacity, not storage.
record.limits_note: Per-object-cap 2 GB. Retention-clamped hard at 48 hours. You cannot request longer. PDFs additionally capped at 50 MB / 1,000 pages for processing. Inline path is 100 MB total request.
record.reliability_note: Documentation states: 'Files are stored for 48 hours. During that time, you can use the API to get metadata about the files. However, you can't download user-uploaded files.' Uploaded files are deleted after 48 hours and cannot be retrieved via API.
